title: Using a Live Analysis System to Study Amyloplast Replication in Arabidopsis Ovule Integuments
author: Makoto T. Fujiwara
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Seeds of transgenic Arabidopsis lines with stable expression of stroma-targeted fluorescent proteins (see General note 1). This protocol presents data from transgenic lines in the Col background [8] and minE [9], and ftsZ triple [10] (hereafter, ftsZ ) mutants, in which a transit peptide (the N-terminal 90 aa of AtFtsZ1-1 [8])-fused YFP is driven by the constitutive CaMV 35S promoter (see Figure 1 ) Figure

Reproductive stages of Arabidopsis suitable for analysis of amyloplast replication. (A) Primary inflorescence. (B) Flower stages 14–17 [11] used for ovule extraction. (C) Expression pattern of CaMV 35S promoter-driven stroma-targeted YFP in a transgenic Arabidopsis line. Images of brightfield (BF) and yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) signals are shown. steps.title: Prepare growth medium and sow seeds
steps.instruction: Prepare Murashige and Skoog medium (pH 5.7) supplemented with 0.1 % MES, 2 % sucrose and 0.7 % agar; sow transgenic Arabidopsis seeds on the medium, stratify in darkness at 4 °C for several days, then expose to light at 23 °C to germinate (1–several days). After germination transfer seedlings to Jiffy‑7 peat pellets pre‑soaked in water and grow under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle of white light at 23 °C for 5–6 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare slides and spacers
steps.instruction: Prepare two glass slides: slide 1 for ovule extraction and slide 2 for microscopy; place 1–3 layers of colored micropore tape on slide 2 to serve as a spacer.

steps.title: Excise flower or silique
steps.instruction: Excise an intact flower or silique from the inflorescence stem of an adult plant.

steps.title: Fix organ on slide
steps.instruction: Place the excised organ on slide 1 and secure the pedicle with a piece of surgical tape so it does not move during dissection.

steps.title: Dissect silique (stages 16–17)
steps.instruction: Using basic tweezers (tweezers 1) under a stereomicroscope at 2.0–3.2× zoom, remove sepals, petals and stamens; optionally peel off one or both valves, then isolate the septum–ovule association.

steps.title: Dissect pistil (stages 13–16)
steps.instruction: Using extra‑fine tweezers (tweezers 2) under a stereomicroscope at 6.3× zoom, remove sepals, petals and stamens; optionally peel off one or both valves, then isolate the septum–ovule association.

steps.title: Mount ovules in liquid
steps.instruction: Apply 40–70 µL of deionized water or liquid Murashige and Skoog medium onto the taped area of slide 2 and transfer the dissected septum–ovule association into the drop.

steps.title: Cover with coverslip and medium
steps.instruction: Gently place a coverslip onto slide 2 and add just enough mounting medium between coverslip and slide to fill the space without excess.

steps.title: Verify ovule integrity
steps.instruction: Observe the preparation at low magnification (e.g., 10× or 20×) using bright‑field microscopy to confirm that ovules are intact.

steps.title: High‑magnification fluorescence observation
steps.instruction: Observe amyloplasts in the outer ovule integument cells with a 60×/1.20 NA water‑immersion objective on a fluorescence microscope.

steps.title: Power on microscope components
steps.instruction: Turn on the halogen lamp, mercury lamp, camera controller (computer) and digital camera.

steps.title: Place slide on microscope
steps.instruction: Place slide 2 on the stage of the inverted fluorescence microscope.

steps.title: Set microscope for YFP detection
steps.instruction: Select the 60× water‑immersion objective (NA 1.20); set the halogen lamp for DIC at 10–50 % output, the mercury lamp for fluorescence at 3–12 % output, insert ND filter 25, and install the YFP filter set (excitation BP490‑500HQ, dichroic FF506‑DiO3, emission FF01‑545/55).

steps.title: Configure camera software
steps.instruction: Start HCImage software; set image mode to 12‑bit, 1920 × 1440 px, binning 1; for single‑image capture set gain 0–255 and exposure 100–500 ms; for time‑lapse set gain 0–255 and exposure 150–500 ms.

steps.title: Focus on ovules with DIC
steps.instruction: Using differential interference contrast optics, focus on individual ovules at 60× through the eyepieces.

steps.title: Acquire images
steps.instruction: Capture images; for time‑lapse microscopy manually maintain focus on individual cells and record up to 60 min, acquiring an image every 30 s or 1 min.
